quizTitle: Operating System Comprehensive Course Work Sample Questions

questions.questionText: The systems which allow only one process execution at a time, are called __________
questions.explanation: Uniprocessing systems allow only one process to execute at a time.

questions.questionText: In operating system, each process has its own __________
options: pending alarms, signals and signal handlers
questions.explanation: Each process has its own address space, global variables, open files, pending alarms, signals, and signal handlers.

questions.questionText: In Unix, Which system call creates the new process?
questions.explanation: The fork system call is used in Unix to create a new process.

questions.questionText: A process can be terminated due to __________
questions.explanation: Processes can terminate normally, due to fatal errors, or by being killed by another process.

questions.questionText: What is the ready state of a process?
options: when process is scheduled to run after some execution
when process is unable to run until some task has been completed
when process is using the CPU
questions.explanation: Ready state means the process is ready to run and waiting for CPU allocation.

questions.questionText: What is interprocess communication?
options: communication between two threads of same process
questions.explanation: Interprocess communication is the mechanism for processes to communicate and synchronize.

questions.questionText: A set of processes is deadlock if __________
options: each process is blocked and will remain so forever
all processes are trying to kill each other
questions.explanation: Deadlock is a state where a set of processes are blocked because each is waiting for a resource held by another.

questions.questionText: A process stack does not contain __________
questions.explanation: A process stack contains temporary data like function parameters, return addresses, and local variables, but not the PID of a child process.

questions.questionText: Which system call can be used by a parent process to determine the termination of child process?
questions.explanation: The wait system call is used by a parent to wait for the termination of a child process.

questions.questionText: The address of the next instruction to be executed by the current process is provided by the __________
questions.explanation: The Program Counter (PC) contains the address of the next instruction to be executed.

questions.questionText: A Process Control Block(PCB) does not contain which of the following?
questions.explanation: PCB contains process state, PC, registers, memory info, etc., but not the bootstrap program which is for system startup.

questions.questionText: The number of processes completed per unit time is known as __________
questions.explanation: Throughput is the number of processes completed per unit time.

questions.questionText: The state of a process is defined by __________
options: the final activity of the process
the activity just executed by the process
the activity to next be executed by the process
the current activity of the process
questions.explanation: The state of a process is defined by its current activity (Running, Ready, Waiting, etc.).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not the state of a process?
questions.explanation: Process states typically include New, Ready, Running, Waiting, Terminated. 'Old' is not a standard state.

questions.questionText: What is a Process Control Block?
questions.explanation: PCB is a data structure used by the OS to store all information about a process.

questions.questionText: The entry of all the PCBs of the current processes is in __________
questions.explanation: The Process Table contains entries for all PCBs of current processes.

questions.questionText: What is the degree of multiprogramming?
options: the number of processes executed per unit time
the number of processes in the ready queue
the number of processes in the I/O queue
the number of processes in memory
questions.explanation: Degree of multiprogramming is the number of processes currently in memory.

questions.questionText: A single thread of control allows the process to perform __________
options: only one task at a time
only two tasks at a time
questions.explanation: A single thread of control means only one task can be performed by the process at a time.

questions.questionText: What is the objective of multiprogramming?
options: Have a process running at all time
Have multiple programs waiting in a queue ready to run
questions.explanation: Multiprogramming aims to increase CPU utilization by always having a process ready to run.

questions.questionText: Which of the following do not belong to queues for processes?
questions.explanation: Standard process queues include Job Queue, Ready Queue, and Device Queue. 'PCB queue' is not a standard term.

questions.questionText: When the process issues an I/O request __________
options: It is placed in an I/O queue
It is placed in a waiting queue
It is placed in the ready queue
It is placed in the Job queue
questions.explanation: When a process issues an I/O request, it is placed in an I/O (or device) queue.

questions.questionText: What will happen when a process terminates?
options: It is removed from all queues
It is removed from all, but the job queue
Its process control block is de-allocated
Its process control block is never de-allocated
questions.explanation: When a process terminates, it is removed from all queues and its PCB is de-allocated.

questions.questionText: What is a long-term scheduler?
options: It selects processes which have to be brought into the ready queue
It selects processes which have to be executed next and allocates CPU
It selects processes which heave to remove from memory by swapping
questions.explanation: The long-term scheduler (job scheduler) selects processes from the job pool and loads them into memory.

questions.questionText: If all processes I/O bound, the ready queue will almost always be ______ and the Short term Scheduler will have a ______ to do.
questions.explanation: If all processes are I/O bound, they spend most of their time waiting for I/O, leaving the ready queue empty and giving the short-term scheduler little work.

questions.questionText: What is a medium-term scheduler?
options: It selects which process has to be brought into the ready queue
It selects which process has to be executed next and allocates CPU
It selects which process to remove from memory by swapping
questions.explanation: The medium-term scheduler handles swapping processes out of and into memory.

questions.questionText: What is a short-term scheduler?
options: It selects which process has to be brought into the ready queue
It selects which process has to be executed next and allocates CPU
It selects which process to remove from memory by swapping
questions.explanation: The short-term scheduler (CPU scheduler) selects which process from the ready queue should be executed next.

questions.questionText: The primary distinction between the short term scheduler and the long term scheduler is __________
options: The type of processes they schedule
questions.explanation: The primary difference is the frequency of execution; short-term runs very often, while long-term runs less frequently.

questions.questionText: The only state transition that is initiated by the user process itself is __________
questions.explanation: A process initiates a 'block' transition (e.g., by requesting I/O). Wakeup and dispatch are initiated by the OS.

questions.questionText: In a time-sharing operating system, when the time slot given to a process is completed, the process goes from the running state to the __________
questions.explanation: In time-sharing, when a time slot expires, the process moves from Running to Ready.

questions.questionText: In a multiprogramming environment __________
options: the processor executes more than one process at a time
the programs are developed by more than one person
more than one process resides in the memory
a single user can execute many programs at the same time
questions.explanation: Multiprogramming environment means more than one process resides in memory at the same time.

questions.questionText: Suppose that a process is in “Blocked” state waiting for some I/O service. When the service is completed, it goes to the __________
questions.explanation: When a blocked process finishes its I/O service, it moves to the Ready state.

questions.questionText: The context of a process in the PCB of a process does not contain __________
options: the value of the CPU registers
questions.explanation: Context of a process includes CPU registers, state, memory info, etc. 'Context switch time' is a performance metric, not stored in the PCB.

questions.questionText: Which of the following need not necessarily be saved on a context switch between processes?
questions.explanation: During a context switch, the Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB) might not need to be saved if the OS handles it separately (e.g., by flushing).

questions.questionText: Which of the following does not interrupt a running process?
questions.explanation: A running process can be interrupted by hardware devices, timers, or power failure. 'Scheduler process' is a software component that runs when the current process is interrupted.

questions.questionText: Which process can be affected by other processes executing in the system?
questions.explanation: Cooperating processes can affect or be affected by other processes executing in the system.

questions.questionText: When several processes access the same data concurrently and the outcome of the execution depends on the particular order in which access takes place is called ________
questions.explanation: A race condition occurs when the outcome depends on the specific order of execution of concurrent processes.

questions.questionText: If a process is executing in its critical section, then no other processes can be executing in their critical section. What is this condition called?
questions.explanation: Mutual exclusion ensures that if one process is in its critical section, no other process can be in theirs.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a synchronization tool?
questions.explanation: A semaphore is a classic synchronization tool used to control access to common resources.

questions.questionText: A semaphore is a shared integer variable __________
options: that can not drop below zero
that can not be more than zero
that can not drop below one
that can not be more than one
questions.explanation: A counting semaphore is a shared integer variable that cannot drop below zero.

questions.questionText: Mutual exclusion can be provided by the __________
options: both mutex locks and binary semaphores
questions.explanation: Both mutex locks and binary semaphores can be used to provide mutual exclusion.

questions.questionText: When high priority task is indirectly preempted by medium priority task effectively inverting the relative priority of the two tasks, the scenario is called __________
questions.explanation: Priority inversion occurs when a high-priority task is blocked by a lower-priority task holding a resource.

questions.questionText: Process synchronization can be done on __________
questions.explanation: Process synchronization can be implemented at both hardware (e.g., test-and-set) and software levels (e.g., semaphores).

questions.questionText: A monitor is a module that encapsulates __________
options: procedures that operate on shared data structure
questions.explanation: A monitor is a high-level synchronization construct that encapsulates shared data, procedures, and synchronization logic.

questions.questionText: To enable a process to wait within the monitor __________
options: a condition variable must be declared as condition
condition variables must be used as boolean objects
questions.explanation: Condition variables (declared as 'condition') are used within monitors to allow processes to wait for specific events.

questions.questionText: Restricting the child process to a subset of the parent’s resources prevents any process from __________
options: overloading the system by using a lot of secondary storage
under-loading the system by very less CPU utilization
overloading the system by creating a lot of sub-processes
crashing the system by utilizing multiple resources
questions.explanation: Restricting child resources prevents a process from overloading the system by creating too many sub-processes.

questions.questionText: A parent process calling _____ system call will be suspended until children processes terminate.
questions.explanation: The wait system call suspends the parent until a child terminates.

questions.questionText: Cascading termination refers to termination of all child processes if the parent process terminates ______
questions.explanation: Cascading termination is the OS-enforced termination of child processes when the parent terminates (normally or abnormally).

questions.questionText: With _____________ only one process can execute at a time; meanwhile all other process are waiting for the processor. With ______________ more than one process can be running simultaneously each on a different processor.
questions.explanation: Uniprocessing allows only one process to run at a time; multiprocessing allows multiple processes to run simultaneously on different processors.

questions.questionText: In UNIX, each process is identified by its __________
questions.explanation: In UNIX, each process is uniquely identified by its Process Identifier (PID).

questions.questionText: In UNIX, the return value for the fork system call is _____ for the child process and _____ for the parent process.
questions.explanation: In UNIX, fork returns 0 to the child and the child's PID (a non-zero integer) to the parent.

questions.questionText: The child process can __________
options: be a duplicate of the parent process
never be a duplicate of the parent process
cannot have another program loaded into it
never have another program loaded into it
questions.explanation: A child process can be a duplicate of the parent (initially) or have a new program loaded into it.

questions.questionText: The child process completes execution, but the parent keeps executing, then the child process is known as __________
questions.explanation: A Zombie process is one that has finished execution but whose entry still exists in the process table because the parent hasn't collected its status.

questions.questionText: What is Interprocess communication?
options: allows processes to communicate and synchronize their actions when using the same address space
allows processes to communicate and synchronize their actions
allows the processes to only synchronize their actions without communication
questions.explanation: Interprocess communication (IPC) allows processes to communicate and synchronize their actions.

questions.questionText: Message passing system allows processes to __________
options: communicate with each other without sharing the same address space
communicate with one another by resorting to shared data
name the recipient or sender of the message
questions.explanation: Message passing allows communication without sharing the same address space.

questions.questionText: Which of the following two operations are provided by the IPC facility?
questions.explanation: IPC facilities provide send and receive message operations for communication.

questions.questionText: Messages sent by a process __________
options: have to be of a fixed size
have to be a variable size
can be fixed or variable sized
questions.explanation: Messages can be of fixed or variable size depending on the system design.

questions.questionText: The link between two processes P and Q to send and receive messages is called __________
questions.explanation: A communication link is the path between two processes for exchanging messages.

questions.questionText: Which of the following are TRUE for direct communication?
options: A communication link can be associated with N number of process(N = max. number of processes supported by system)
A communication link is associated with exactly two processes
Exactly N/2 links exist between each pair of processes(N = max. number of processes supported by system)
Exactly two link exists between each pair of processes
questions.explanation: Direct communication requires each process to explicitly name the recipient or sender, creating a link associated with exactly two processes.

questions.questionText: In indirect communication between processes P and Q __________
options: there is another process R to handle and pass on the messages between P and Q
there is another machine between the two processes to help communication
there is a mailbox to help communication between P and Q
questions.explanation: Indirect communication uses mailboxes or ports to help processes communicate.

questions.questionText: In the non blocking send __________
options: the sending process keeps sending until the message is received
the sending process sends the message and resumes operation
the sending process keeps sending until it receives a message
questions.explanation: In non-blocking send, the sender sends the message and continues with its execution without waiting.

questions.questionText: In the Zero capacity queue __________
options: the queue can store at least one message
the sender blocks until the receiver receives the message
the sender keeps sending and the messages don’t wait in the queue

questions.questionText: The Zero Capacity queue __________
options: is referred to as a message system with buffering
is referred to as a message system with no buffering
is referred to as a link

questions.questionText: Bounded capacity and Unbounded capacity queues are referred to as __________
Remote Procedure Calls are used ____________
options: for communication between two processes remotely different from each other on the same system
for communication between two processes on the same system
for communication between two processes on separate systems

questions.questionText: To differentiate the many network services a system supports ______ are used.
RPC provides a(an) _____ on the client-side, a separate one for each remote procedure.
What is stub?
options: transmits the message to the server where the server side stub receives the message and invokes procedure on the server side
packs the parameters into a form transmittable over the network
locates the port on the server

questions.questionText: To resolve the problem of data representation on different systems RPCs define _____________
The remote method invocation __________
options: allows a process to invoke memory on a remote object
allows a thread to invoke a method on a remote object
allows a thread to invoke memory on a remote object
allows a process to invoke a method on a remote object

questions.questionText: A process that is based on IPC mechanism which executes on different systems and can communicate with other processes using message based communication, is called ________
The initial program that is run when the computer is powered up is called __________
How does the software trigger an interrupt?
options: Sending signals to CPU through bus
Executing a special operation called system call
Executing a special program called system program
Executing a special program called interrupt trigger program

questions.questionText: What is a trap/exception?
options: hardware generated interrupt caused by an error
software generated interrupt caused by an error
user generated interrupt caused by an error

questions.questionText: What is an ISR?
What is an interrupt vector?
options: It is an address that is indexed to an interrupt handler
It is a unique device number that is indexed by an address
It is a unique identity given to an interrupt

questions.questionText: DMA is used for __________
options: High speed devices(disks and communications network)

questions.questionText: In a memory mapped input/output __________
options: the CPU uses polling to watch the control bit constantly, looping to see if a device is ready
the CPU writes one data byte to the data register and sets a bit in control register to show that a byte is available
the CPU receives an interrupt when the device is ready for the next byte
the CPU runs a user written code and does accordingly

questions.questionText: In a programmed input/output(PIO) __________
options: the CPU uses polling to watch the control bit constantly, looping to see if a device is ready
the CPU writes one data byte to the data register and sets a bit in control register to show that a byte is available
the CPU receives an interrupt when the device is ready for the next byte
the CPU runs a user written code and does accordingly

questions.questionText: In an interrupt driven input/output __________
options: the CPU uses polling to watch the control bit constantly, looping to see if a device is ready
the CPU writes one data byte to the data register and sets a bit in control register to show that a byte is available
the CPU receives an interrupt when the device is ready for the next byte
the CPU runs a user written code and does accordingly

questions.questionText: In the layered approach of Operating Systems __________
options: Bottom Layer(0) is the User interface
Highest Layer(N) is the User interface

questions.questionText: How does the Hardware trigger an interrupt?
options: Sending signals to CPU through a system bus
Executing a special program called interrupt program
Executing a special program called system program
Executing a special operation called system call

questions.questionText: Which operation is performed by an interrupt handler?
options: Saving the current state of the system
Loading the interrupt handling code and executing it
Once done handling, bringing back the system to the original state it was before the interrupt occurred

options: CPU is allocated to the process with highest priority
CPU is allocated to the process with lowest priority

classification of ready queue is permanent
processes are not classified into groups

questions.questionText: Which one of the following can not be scheduled by the kernel?

With multiprogramming ______ is used productively.
What are the two steps of a process execution?

options: a few very short CPU bursts
a few very short I/O bursts

questions.questionText: A process is selected from the ______ queue by the ________ scheduler, to be executed.
In the following cases non – preemptive scheduling occurs?
options: When a process switches from the running state to the ready state
When a process goes from the running state to the waiting state
When a process switches from the waiting state to the ready state

questions.questionText: The switching of the CPU from one process or thread to another is called ____________
What is Dispatch latency?
options: the speed of dispatching a process from running to the ready state
the time of dispatching a process from running to ready state and keeping the CPU idle
the time to stop one process and start running another one

questions.questionText: Scheduling is done so as to ____________
Scheduling is done so as to ____________
options: increase the duration of a specific amount of work

questions.questionText: What is Turnaround time?
options: the total waiting time for a process to finish execution
the total time spent in the ready queue
the total time spent in the running queue
the total time from the completion till the submission of a process

questions.questionText: Scheduling is done so as to ____________
options: there is no relation between scheduling and turnaround time

questions.questionText: What is Waiting time?
options: the total time in the blocked and waiting queues
the total time spent in the ready queue
the total time spent in the running queue
the total time from the completion till the submission of a process

questions.questionText: Scheduling is done so as to ____________
options: keep the waiting time the same

questions.questionText: What is Response time?
options: the total time taken from the submission time till the completion time
the total time taken from the submission time till the first response is produced
the total time taken from submission time till the response is output

questions.questionText: Round robin scheduling falls under the category of ____________

using very small time slices converts it into First come First served scheduling algorithm

questions.questionText: The portion of the process scheduler in an operating system that dispatches processes is concerned with ____________
options: assigning ready processes to waiting queue
assigning running processes to blocked queue

questions.questionText: Complex scheduling algorithms ____________
options: are very appropriate for very large computers

questions.questionText: What is FIFO algorithm?
options: first executes the job that came in last in the queue
first executes the job that came in first in the queue
first executes the job that needs minimal processor
first executes the job that has maximum processor needs

its scheduling takes up a lot of time
it can lead to some low priority process waiting indefinitely for the CPU

questions.questionText: What is ‘Aging’?
options: keeping track of what pages are currently residing in memory
keeping track of how many times a given page is referenced
increasing the priority of jobs to ensure termination in a finite time

options: after a process has made a request to enter its critical section and before the request is granted
